The eye is clearly visible, large, and positioned laterally on the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wide mouth with protruding lower jaw.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the mouth is wide, the jaw structure resembles that of a Pike (duck-bill shape) rather than the specific protruding lower jaw morphology of a Snoek. The tongue/lower lip area appears somewhat fused or indistinct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated streamlined body with notably extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is distinctly elongated and cylindrical, fitting the general description of the class.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small silvery scales with bluish-green dorsal coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish displays a dark green/brown back with distinct light yellowish/white bean-shaped spots along the flank. This pattern is diagnostic for Northern Pike, whereas Barracouta are generally uniform silvery-grey with small scales and no such spotting.
A lateral line is faintly visible running along the side of the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Separated dorsal fins; first dorsal spiny, second dorsal soft-rayed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible dorsal fin is single and located far back on the body near the tail, which is characteristic of Pike. Barracouta have two separated dorsal fins situated more centrally/anteriorly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anal fin similar to second dorsal.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: An anal fin is visible opposite the dorsal fin, consistent with the visible anatomy (though the anatomy itself is wrong for the class).
The caudal fin is forked, consistent with the visual evidence.
